To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) existing models of implicit regularizers in the supervised learning setting do not apply to the temporal difference learning setting; (2) the implicit regularizer derived from these models in the temporal difference setting favors degenerate feature representations; and (3) we derive the form for this implicit regularizer, and use it to propose a simple and highly effective explicit regularizer called DR3 that counteracts its undesirable effects.

(1) existing models of implicit regularizer for supervised learning do not generalize to offline deep reinforcement learning and (2) a new explicit regularizer, DR3, can be derived to counteract the undesirable effects of implicit regularization in offline deep reinforcement learning, improving the generalization of learned representations.
(1) implicit regularization in deep RL is harmful, and (2) explicit regularization in the form of DR3 improves performance and stability in offline RL.
